title: Live output coalescing and heuristic reconnect for SSE streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Clients using Server-Sent Events (SSE) to stream tokens experience high HTTP and TLS overhead when the server emits many tiny chunks (single-token or per-functioncall tokens). Additionally, transient network blips cause clients to reconnect and may replay or lose partially received structured outputs (JSON arrays, function call payloads).

Goal: Implement a server-side coalescing layer that groups small outgoing frames into larger SSE events while preserving low-latency delivery for interactive workloads, and a heuristic reconnect/resume behavior that maximizes successful continuation without breaking existing client compatibility. The feature must preserve semantics for function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs, be opt-in behind a feature flag and header, and be gradually rolled out with observability and safety knobs.
acceptance_criteria: Average SSE event size increases by at least 4x for streaming sessions with token-per-chunk behavior, without increasing 99th-percentile token latency by more than 10ms for interactive sessions
Clients that reconnect within 20s should resume from the correct logical token boundary >= 95% of the time (measured in synthetic test harness)
No regression in function/tool-calling compatibility: function call payloads must remain parseable as single JSON objects by the SDKs
All changes behind feature flag and server returns a header X-RW-SSE-Coalesce: enabled when active
Automated integration tests for JS and Python SDKs validating resume, dedupe and structured output correctness
Canary rollout metrics show duplicate chunk ratio < 0.5% and stream error rate not increased compared to baseline
implementation_steps: Write RFC describing coalescing heuristics, chunk metadata, and resume token format (include backward-compatibility section)
Add a Coalescer in the runtime output pipeline: buffer small frames for up to coalesce_time_ms or until coalesce_size_bytes reached
Emit per-SSE-event metadata in a comment prefixed line (e.g., :meta id=... seq=... last-logical-offset=...) to avoid breaking simple SSE parsers
Introduce a resume token format: base64(model_run_id + "!" + connection_seq + "/" + byte_offset) and document parsing rules
Make chunk IDs deterministic per-stream (monotonic sequence) so servers and clients can dedupe on resume
Ensure function-call objects are marked with an 'fc_boundary' flag to force flush the coalescer immediately so function payloads are emitted as discrete JSON objects
Add server-side validation to reject resumption attempts that cross incompatible model-run IDs
Expose config knobs: coalesce_time_ms (default 40ms), coalesce_size_bytes (default 8k), force_flush_on_function_call=true
Add metrics and tracing spans: chunk_coalesce_ratio, resume_attempts, resume_successes, duplicate_chunks_detected
Implement unit and integration tests; fuzz malformed meta lines to verify client robustness
Feature-flag and rollout path: infra flag + API query param ?sse_coalesce=1 for immediate testing
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Coalescing improves throughput and reduces CPU/TLS overhead but adds small buffering latency. We choose a conservative default coalesce_time_ms=40ms to favor interactivity over maximum aggregation.

Embedding metadata as SSE comment lines (beginning with ':') keeps standard SSE parsers happy and avoids changing event payload format, at cost of requiring SDKs to parse those comments to reconstruct resume semantics.

Resume token encodes model_run_id to avoid resuming across different model instances that may have divergent deterministic outputs; this prevents subtle content shifts at the expense of spurious resume failures when backend switches model behind the scenes.
Force-flushing on function/tool calling preserves compatibility with existing SDKs expecting function call JSON to be present in a single chunk; we prefer this to complex JSON-reassembly on clients.
We avoid introducing new HTTP endpoints for resume to minimize infra changes; resume happens over normal SSE connection handshake with Last-Event-ID and a resume token header.
Security: resume tokens are opaque and short-lived to reduce replay risk. We will not place PII into tokens.
testing_plan: Unit tests for coalescer thresholds and immediate flush behavior (function call boundaries)
Integration tests with JS SDK and Python SDK using real SSE parser to validate event ordering and structured JSON reassembly
Network partition simulation: kill TCP mid-stream, reconnect with resume token, assert correctness on server-side dedupe and client-visible output
Chaos test harness: random latency and packet drops with 10k synthetic sessions to measure resume_success_rate and duplicate chunk rate
Backward-compat compatibility suite: verify simple curl + EventSource clients (that ignore comment meta-lines) still receive valid event payloads
Security fuzzing on resume token parsing and header injection to ensure invalid tokens are safely rejected
rollout_and_migration: Deploy behind infra feature flag and an API-visible header. Start with developer-only endpoints and internal SDK dogfood.
Canary: 1% traffic for 48 hours -> 10% traffic for 72 hours -> 50% for 7 days -> 100%
If duplicate_chunks_detected > 0.5% or resume_success_rate < 90%, rollback the feature flag and open incident
Provide clients with guidance: SDKs will parse comment meta lines automatically; non-upgraded clients will still receive valid streams but without resume guarantees
After stable rollout, flip default feature flag on for all hosted customers and expose config for Dedicated/Private installs
observability: Tracing: add span 'sse.coalesce' with attributes: coalesce_count, total_bytes, flushed_reason
Log warnings when resumption fails with diagnostic codes (INCOMPAT_MODEL, BAD_TOKEN, OUT_OF_WINDOW)
Dashboards: new panel in Console under 'API Streaming' to view coalesce effects and resume health
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Some third-party SSE clients drop comment lines or treat them differently. Mitigation: keep event payload intact and only put metadata in comment lines; document behavior and provide SDK updates.
Risk: Resume tokens leak information. Mitigation: opaque base64 encoding, short TTL, no user data embedded.
Risk: Coalescing hides function-call boundaries leading to unparsable JSON. Mitigation: immediate flush on function-call boundary and additional sentinel in comment meta.

Risk: Increased memory pressure from buffering many high-throughput streams. Mitigation: per-connection coalesce_size cap and global circuit breaker that disables coalescing when memory pressure crosses threshold.
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket with RFC draft attached. Initial proposal uses 40ms/8k defaults. Requesting design review from Marco and Lina.
2025-02-11 - Marco Nguyen: Reviewed RFC; suggested using SSE comment lines for metadata and clarified resume token encoding. Asked for explicit force-flush on function call boundaries.

2025-02-12 - Lina Chen: Flagged potential issue with third-party SSE libs that strip comments. Lina suggested adding an optional HTTP header on handshake with resume-capability boolean so non-upgraded clients can be detected.
2025-02-14 - Marco Nguyen: Implemented coalescer skeleton and added unit tests for immediate flush. Observed a 3.8x average event size increase during local benchmarking.
2025-02-15 - QA Bot: Integration tests run on staging; found 0.9% duplicate chunk rate in stress test. Investigating dedupe window sizing.
